subject: DPA clarifications: controller/processor, subprocessors, breach notice

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>

Cc: Ethan Li <ethan.li@acme-payments.com>
Date: Sun, 15 Feb 2026 18:02:00 -0800
Subject: DPA clarifications: controller/processor, subprocessors, breach notice

Hi Sofia—thanks again for the call today. Quick recap and a couple of follow-ups so your legal/privacy team has everything for review:

1) Roles: We discussed Redwood acting as processor for customer data sent to our hosted API; customer (Acme Payments) would be the controller for end-customer PII. If you'd like us to accept controller-level obligations for any hosted feature, let me know but that typically requires a tailored contract.

2) Subprocessors: I attached our current subprocessors export (CSV) and a short summary doc. We run inference on GPUs in AWS regions and use a logging/CDN partner for audit logs. Subprocessor additions are communicated 30 days in advance in our DPA.

3) Breach notice & incident handling: Our standard DPA commits to 72-hour initial notification for security incidents that materially affect customer data, plus a post-incident report. For highly regulated workflows we can agree on tighter SLAs — we'll need legal to sign off.

Next steps: Could you confirm the two items your team raised on the call: (A) whether Acme requires data residency (EU/US) for token storage and (B) whether Acme needs us to list a specific set of subprocessors in the DPA rather than referencing a dynamic list? I can loop in our security/legal leads and provide proposed language for the DPA.

I've attached Redwood_DPA_Summary_v1.2.pdf and the subprocessors CSV. Happy to set a short follow-up with legal if helpful.

Best,
Marissa
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.ai | +1 415-555-0192

Attachments: Redwood_DPA_Summary_v1.2.pdf (summary), subprocessors_list_2026-02.csv (export)
From: Sofia Navarro <sofia.navarro@acme-payments.com>

Subject: Re: DPA clarifications: controller/processor, subprocessors, breach notice

Thanks Marissa — this is helpful. A few follow-ups from our privacy team: 

- Controller vs. Processor: Confirming Acme will be controller for transaction PII. We also need to confirm Redwood will process aggregated telemetry (model usage metrics) as processor only and will not attempt to re-identify any PII. Is that covered in your standard DPA?

- Subprocessors: Our procurement lead prefers a static list in the DPA rather than a dynamic reference if there are subprocessors that store data persistently. Can Redwood commit to listing persistent-data subprocessors in the contract?

- Breach notice: 72 hours initial notice is acceptable as long as it includes the scope of affected data and remediation plan within 7 days. Also need a contact for SOC 2 evidence and proof of past audits.

Can you loop in your security/legal and procurement contact and share the proposed contract language?

--
Sofia Navarro
Head of Privacy & Compliance, Acme Payments

From: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.ai>

Subject: Re: DPA clarifications: controller/processor, subprocessors, breach notice

Hi all — quick answers and recommended contract language in-line below. Attaching a redline (DPA_redline_for_Acme_2026-02.pdf) to this thread; Marissa, adding to attachments list.

1) Controller/Processor: Confirmed — Acme is controller; Redwood is processor. Proposed language: "Customer is the Controller and Redwood Inference is the Processor with respect to Customer Data as defined in Section 1.1. Redwood shall process Customer Data only on documented instructions from Customer and shall not attempt to re-identify or deanonymize PII."

2) Subprocessors: For subprocessors that persistently store Customer Data (e.g., logging/storage partners), Redwood can provide a static annex listing those subprocessors at contract signing and will notify the customer of any additions 30 days prior to engagement. Proposed clause: "Redwood shall list Persistent Subprocessors in Annex A. Redwood will provide 30 days notice before adding any new Persistent Subprocessor and will provide reasonable opportunity for Customer to object."

3) Breach notice: We confirm 72-hour initial notification for qualifying incidents and a follow-up remediation/status summary within 7 calendar days. SOC 2 evidence: we can share an encrypted read-only link to the latest SOC 2 Type II report after an NDA or an executed DPA. Proposed clause: "Redwood shall notify Customer without undue delay and in any event within 72 hours of becoming aware of a Security Incident materially affecting Customer Data and shall provide a remediation plan within 7 days. Redwood may provide SOC 2 evidence subject to mutual NDA/confidentiality obligations."

Let me know if Acme has additional must-have language. If approved, legal can prepare the redline to feed into procurement.

Thanks,
Aditya Rao
Head of Security & Compliance, Redwood Inference
aditya.rao@redwood.ai
